description:
FILED s511 (Fable, 2026-10-07) from the r/perl discussion with brian d foy ("Are you sure you can detect it? eval $dont_know_what_this_is;").  Probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s511/review/eval-protos/p*.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main 3ea47a41 (d2f7e757 records).

THE GAP: the text of a string eval is compiled with FOUR facts -- the text, the caller's package, the captured lexical NAMES, the features in force (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the p-eval cache-key comment) -- and NO sub table.  So inside an eval string every sub of the ENCLOSING program is an unknown bareword, even one that is perfectly static in the main file, and the prototype-driven parse is lost:
    sub un3 ($) { "u:$_[0]" }          print eval(q{join "|", un3 1, 2})          perl u:1|2   PCL u:1        (p16, SILENT)
    *un2 = sub ($) {...};                print eval(q{join "|", un2 1, 2})          perl u:1|2   PCL u:1        (p13, SILENT)
    eval q{sub un ($) {...}};            print eval(q{join "|", un 1, 2})           perl u:1|2   PCL u:1        (p12, SILENT)
    use Scalar::Util qw(blessed);         eval q{blessed $o && $o->isa("K") ? "yes" : "no"}   perl yes   PCL undef, $@ empty   (p25, SILENT -- the realistic one)
    use List::Util qw(first);             eval q{first { $_ > 1 } 1, 2, 3}          perl 2       PCL drop, $@ set (p19, p18 via require+import, p11 via an eval-defined (&@) sub)
    use List::Util qw(max);               eval q{max 1, 7, 3}                        perl 7       PCL 7 (right by luck: unknown word + term = list call)
    use List::Util qw(max) INSIDE the eval text                                      perl 5       PCL 5 (p14: what the eval text itself `use`s IS read)
The same family already filed piecemeal: #2768 (a constant is not a TERM inside an eval -- p15/p20 reproduce it), #2610 (set_prototype in BEGIN, incl. its eval half), #1509 (a module's eval-built prototype invisible to the caller).  The ruling that names the horizon: DECIDED "THE STRING-EVAL HORIZON IS WHERE A COMPILE-TIME RULE HAS TO STOP" (the handle-vs-call question deferred to run time with the :expr-slot mode).  This task is the prototype half of that horizon: ( $ ) named-unary and scalar imposition, (&@) block form, () term -- for subs DECLARED, glob-ASSIGNED or IMPORTED by the program.

ANSWER TO #2610's "cheap discriminating measurement": nothing run-time reaches the eval compile today -- and nothing STATIC either (p16: a plain `sub un3 ($)` in the main file).  So the fix is one channel for both halves.

FIX SHAPE (not designed in detail): the eval request gains the (name -> prototype text) pairs of the subs visible in the eval's package at the moment of the eval, read from the runtime's live registry (%pcl-sub-prototypes is what prototype() reads; a sub with no prototype is a plain list call and need not be sent -- except where the compiler would otherwise take the built-in's rule, #2779) -- the same channel the capture names ride (#296-B1), and the same discipline: a capture-dependent emission must KEY THE EVAL CACHE (s387), so the pairs join the cache key (text + package + capture names + features + prototype pairs).  Constants (#2768) come for free: a `()` prototype pair makes the name a term.  Measure the request size on JSON::PP's 80 evals before shipping (every visible sub's prototype, or only the prototyped ones).

NOT fixable by this: a sub installed by BEGIN-time code and used by the FILE's own later statements (#2610's detector; the compiler parsed those before anything ran).

WHAT IS RIGHT TODAY, for the record (probed, identical to perl): a definition at ordinary run time never changes how the FILE parses (p9: `sub bar; eval q{sub bar ($)...}; bar 1, 2` = b:1 2 in both); a pragma imported inside an eval does not leak out (p23); a sub whose name is later used as a class name (p24); `BEGIN { require M; M->import(LIST) }` with an explicit list (p21).

=== s512 NOTE (Fable, 2026-10-07): the RUN-TIME half, probed ===  `*g = sub ($) { 7 }; my $n = eval 'my @r = (g 1, 2); scalar @r'; print $n` -- perl 2 (the eval's compile sees the sub table AS IT IS AT RUN TIME, so a run-time glob assignment's prototype governs the eval), PCL 1 (probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s512/review/static/p07-evalproto).  The static half (this task: prototype pairs ride the request) fixes the declared/imported case; the run-time case needs the runtime's OWN table at eval time -- #2610's detector family.  Review: docs/static-parse-limits-review-s512.md family A.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a prototyped sub of the ENCLOSING program (declared `sub f ($)`, glob-assigned, or IMPORTED -- Scalar::Util::blessed, List::Util::first) is parsed as a plain list operator inside a STRING EVAL; the eval request carries no sub table at all (not even the main file's static declarations) -- `eval q{blessed $o && $o->isa("K") ? "yes" : "no"}` is undef, perl yes
